## Epic A — Reverse-engineer and rebuild Overworld (2006 VB.NET/DirectX prototype) in Unity
- **U.OVW-US-A1 ✅** As the owner, the project is built on engine-free foundations: Overworld.Core (pure C#, noEngineReferences) holds the rules and changes only through commands that carry a player id and produce events, Overworld.Runtime, Overworld.Editor and the test assemblies reference it one way, and the simulation steps at a fixed 60 Hz so the original's per-frame speeds behave identically on any machine (RECONSTRUCTION sections 2 and 19).
- **U.OVW-US-A2 ⬜** As the owner, every number and string the original kept in data or hard-coded in its source lives in validated data files loaded by Core: both world.mdb databases (the engine's data/world.mdb and the later root world.mdb), hero.mdb, the five books, the 372 original pickups and the restored Nitro Bean, the quests and subquests, the two weapons, the three heroes, and the walls and props, with a test that loads them and cross-checks them against RECONSTRUCTION sections 8, 10 and 16.
- **U.OVW-US-A3 ✅** As the owner, all 895 original files (gfx, sfx, data, executable and databases) are catalogued in the repo with a disposition (imported and used, imported and used by the union layer, or recorded and deliberately not shipped), and a test diffs the catalogue against the original's file list so no asset is silently missing (RECONSTRUCTION section 17).
- **U.OVW-US-A4 ✅** As a player, I see the world as the original drew it: an 11 by 11 grid of 512-pixel area tiles (A1 to F8, one world unit per tile, row A at the top) seen through a 45-degree perspective camera that looks straight down the Z axis from -1 and zooms out to -3.5, everything beyond the render range culled, a magenta-cleared backdrop box behind it, and heroes, tree-trunk props and weapons drawn back to front by Y.
- **U.OVW-US-A5 ✅** As a player, I move my hero by holding the right mouse button toward the cursor (walking when the cursor is near, running when it is far or the run key is held and stamina remains, slowing to a stop on arrival), or with the arrow keys, with the original's 0.003/0.006 walk and run speeds, 0.001 acceleration steps, four-way facing, and the six-frame walk and run cycles of Chrono at 64 pixels.
- **U.OVW-US-A6 ⬜** As a player, the mouse is a world cursor with the original's arrow, edge-scroll arrows, zoom and eye (examine) sprites: moving it to a screen edge scrolls the camera (three times as fast with Shift) within the original's limits around the hero, the camera eases back to centre on the hero while I move, the wheel or middle button zooms between -1 and -3.5, and F, the numpad and X/Z give the free-camera and isometric debug moves.
- **U.OVW-US-A7 ✅** As a player, six hard-coded wall segments (the horizontal, vertical and angled runs from (1,0) to (4,2)) stop my heroes from walking through them exactly as the original's collision pushed them back, and a hero recalled to the party falls into place from Z -1.
- **U.OVW-US-A8 ✅** As a player, I lead a party of three (Chrono, Belmont and Flagg, all on Chrono's sprites) that follows me: followers run when over 0.2 units away, walk when near, stand within 0.05, are recalled beside me beyond 1 unit, separate when they crowd each other, and I switch leader with [ and ] or a left click on a hero, with the Team/Solo button (apostrophe or the panel) turning following off so the others kneel.
- **U.OVW-US-A9 ✅** As a player, the game has a clock that runs one in-game minute per real second from 9:00 AM on 1 January of year 64, divides the day into Day (9 to 18), Evening (18 to 21), Night (21 to 6) and Morning (6 to 9) with the original's ambient tints and fade steps, announces each period on screen, names the months and weekdays with the original's fantasy calendar, and shows the time and date on the HUD and hero screen.
- **U.OVW-US-A10 ✅** As a player, each hero has health, mana and stamina with the original's maximums (50, 20 and 60), regenerates and spends stamina as the original does (plus 1 standing, plus 2 kneeling, minus 1 running, every 2 seconds), shows the Exhausted, Angry or Poisoned status animation above them when stamina is under 15 percent, health under 5 percent or poisoned, loses a health point every 2 seconds while poisoned, and sees all of it on the status box and the three bottom-left bars.
- **U.OVW-US-A11 ✅** As a player, I can rest: the rest key kneels me, again lays me down, and while laid I set 1 to 24 hours with left/down and right/up and confirm to sleep, which fades the screen out, restores one-eighth of maximum health, mana and stamina per hour for the whole party (stamina not while poisoned), advances the clock and fades back in, and the Moon Berry and Morningstar sleep until 10 PM and 5 AM.
- **U.OVW-US-A12 ✅** As a player, I find and pick up the original's 372 pickups (plus the restored Nitro Bean as a 373rd, per the BIBLE) at their placements (the named herbs, the 45-plant potato and 49-plant turnip fields, the sword, books, rune, cheese, apple, eggs, coffee and nitro beans, and the randomly scattered gold, 5-gold and satchels), with a name label on the nearest one in reach (0.05), comma and period (or the wheel) cycling among those in reach, picking up kneeling the hero, picked-up herbs and crops growing back after their growth time, gold and satchels paying out at once, and the E key opening the examine box for the one under the cursor.
- **U.OVW-US-A13 ✅** As a player, I carry what I pick up in the inventory panel: stacked by name, ten icons per row with a cursor, weight against the party limit (28.5) kneeling me when over-burdened, swapping items with the run key, dropping them back into the world (and picking the drops up again), using them on a chosen party member or on myself, reusable items surviving use, the Delete key and panel button toggling it, and the 1 to 0 keys using items from the quick bar.
- **U.OVW-US-A14 ✅** As a player, I can type the original's scripting language into the tilde console (CHANGE, MOVE and RUN commands over HERO, CAMERA, TIME, LIGHT, INVENTORY, BOOK, OPTIONS, CURSOR and SCRIPT, compound with ' | ', arithmetic with +/- and assignment otherwise), Insert recalls the last one, and every item's effect, the Rune's teleport and the quest end scripts run through it, with errors reported on screen as 'Script failed to execute.' and exceptions as 'Script failed to run.'
- **U.OVW-US-A15 ✅** As a player, I follow the original's four main quests (Farmer Brinn's fields, the centre field, the west-east pair and the far west) and two subquests, walking into each objective's range to complete it and earn the original's experience values, with the quest screen on Page Down (main, subquests, finished tabs) and a marker drawn in the world at every incomplete objective.
- **U.OVW-US-A16 ✅** As a player, I read the five books (Grimoire de'Alchemiste, Dragon Almanac, Poetry Book, Matt's Book, Colesium Vol I) in a two-page book view with the original's covers, fonts and Roman page numbers, turning pages with left/right or the wheel and cycling books with N, opening a book from its inventory item or the B key.
- **U.OVW-US-A17 ✅** As a player, the world has its weather and scenery: 2,501 particles of snow, rain, falling leaves and dust storm, cycled with W (starting in snow), 401 drifting clouds with four balloons, the tent at (-0.7,-0.04) and the four props, all falling, drifting and recycling as the original does.
- **U.OVW-US-A18 ✅** As a player, I toggle battle mode with End: heroes draw their weapon with the original's draw and battle animations (the Steel Sword for Belmont and Flagg, the Fine Axe for Chrono, with their overlay sprites kept in step), the leader's stamina becomes a turn gauge that recharges kneeling at the original's 0.18-second rate, a hero reaching full is Ready and draws, and the team enters and leaves battle together.
- **U.OVW-US-A19 ✅** As a player, in battle I choose from the ring menu around the active hero (Move, End, Skill, Item, Attack; rotated with left/right or the wheel, pulsed with Up, chosen with Enter or click), Move lets me walk only as far as my stamina allows (agility times 0.05 units, shown as a dotted circle), Attack shows my weapon's range circle, Item opens the inventory at a 10 percent stamina cost, a pickup costs 5 percent, and End or running out of stamina passes the turn to the next ready hero with the camera following.
- **U.OVW-US-A20 ⬜** As a player, the interface is complete: fading status messages, the tutorial text on start, the F11 options menu (controls list and exit), the PageUp hero screen, the FPS counter, the pause banner, the 12 random loading screens, the team, inventory and turn-bar widgets, and the eye cursor in examine mode.
- **U.OVW-US-A21 ⬜** As a player, I can play with a gamepad: the left stick moves and the buttons run, pick up, open the inventory, rest, drop and switch hero as in the original's button map (J toggles it).
- **U.OVW-US-A22 ⬜** As a player, the game has sound: the music track plays and loops (the original constructed it but never played it), and the footsteps, jump, sword draw, swing and hit, defend, charge, regen, death and ambient zombies sounds are wired to the events they were evidently made for, with the original's music, effect and ambient volumes and the F7/F8 regen test.
- **U.OVW-US-A23 ⬜** As a player, the game remembers its window, resolution and colour depth between runs as the original did in its registry key, shows the first-run welcome, and F12 toggles between windowed and full screen without losing the game.
- **U.OVW-US-A24 ⬜** As a player, when the current hero's health reaches zero the screen fades to black and the game resets (pickups returned, inventory emptied, the day period set to Morning with the clock unchanged, the camera home) as the original's GameOver and Reset do, with the original's never-restored health defect replaced by restoring the party.
- **U.OVW-US-A25 ⬜** As a player, the later world design is playable: the root world.mdb areas Grasslands and Lowlands with their eight landscape scenes, sky strips and mountain layer in parallax, the nine terrain segments the heroes walk over, and the placed orchard trees, Stonehenge and the Gateway from its prop table.
- **U.OVW-US-A26 ⬜** As a player, stepping into a data-defined event box runs its script, so the Poison Box hurts, the Healing Box heals and Entering Dark Woods turns the day to night, at the rate the data gives, and the older database's three events (Test, Dark Woods, Cinematic) and three scripts are kept as data.
- **U.OVW-US-A27 ⬜** As a player, I meet the Peasant Woman (standing) and the Magitek Armor (pursuing) placed in Grasslands, drawn with their walking, left, right and front sprites at 0.144 by 0.072.
- **U.OVW-US-A28 ⬜** As a player, I meet the data-defined enemies (Werelynx, Botherfly, Blue Slime, Red Slime, Toadie) with their health, speed, sensing range, state (passive, aggressive, afraid, defensive), motion (walking, flying, hopping) and class, drawn with the catman and slime sprites in stand, walk, attack and hurt poses, with the original's missing art (Botherfly, Toadie) supplied as placeholders flagged for replacement.
- **U.OVW-US-A29 ⬜** As a player, attacking and being attacked works: weapon rating, slashing, piercing and blunt values, range and durability (Steel Sword 28 of 30, Fine Axe 41 of 50), enemy health and class, defeat, and the Axe, Steel Sword, Katana and Broad Sword of the hero database, resolved by Core commands and events, with every number a documented decision because the original had no damage code.
- **U.OVW-US-A30 ⬜** As a player, I can equip heroes from the hero database (Alexander, health 50, strength 1, agility 2, speed 2, with the Steel Sword), its four weapons with their sprite sets, and the empty head, body, arms and feet armour and relic slots, on a hero screen.
- **U.OVW-US-A31 ⬜** As a player, I can choose the Belmont or girl sprite pack for a hero (the original's unused stand, walk, run, jump, dash, kneel and attack sets), kept as selectable art with the facings the engine uses.
- **U.OVW-US-A32 ⬜** As the owner, the original's unfinished hooks exist as defined seams so nothing in the original is dropped: the five spell schools and the Flame spell behind the Skill ring entry, the cutscene record, the Mechanical enemy class and the Teleporting, Stationary and Swimming motions, and the Item_Textures table.
- **U.OVW-US-A33 ⬜** As the owner, the finished game is verified end to end by a scripted run that plays every mechanic against RECONSTRUCTION.md and captures screenshots, with the Windows build launching, so the repo can be called a complete proof of concept of the original.
